p:cNvPr.descr: Left: A fully saturated fatty acid, shown two ways. On the left is a Kekule structure, with a long hydrocarbon chain (labeled left) bonded up to a C, which double bonds up & right to O and up and left to O-. To the right is a ball structure of a fatty acid. It is a long chain of charcoal gray balls, representing the carbon chain. The two red balls at the top, oriented right, represent the carbonyl group. Right, unsaturated fatty acid, shown two ways. On the left is a Kekule structure with the long hydrocarbon chain bonded up to C which double bonds up and right to O and up and left to O-. The difference is in the now-present double bond between the 8th and 9th carbons down from the carbonyl group. It is in the cis configuration, where it forms a plateau shape with the two bonds to either side of it, as opposed to a zigzag shape. The bond is shown in red. To the right is the ball structure, which is a long chain of charcoal gray balls, representing the carbon chain. Some distance down the chain, it bends and kinks to the left due to the cis double bond.

p:cNvPr.descr: This is a comparison of the structures of glycerol and trialcylglycerol, with Kekule structures and ball models. At the top of the diagram is a Kekule structure of glycerol, shaded orange. Glycerol's carbons are numbered beginning on the left. C1 is part of CH2, which bonds down and left to OH, and down and right to C2, which is part of CH. CH bonds down to OH and right and up to C3, which is part of CH2, and bonds down and right to OH. Below is a ball model of triacylglycerol, shown as two long, charcoal gray carbon chains with a curved carbon chain in the middle. They converge at the top where there are 2 red atoms that represent oxygen. Below is the Kekule structure of triacylglycerol. The glycerol chain, shaded orange, is the central portion. C1 bonds left to O, which bonds left to C, which double bonds up and left to O and down to a long carbon chain. C2 bonds down to O, which bonds down to C, which double bonds up and left to O, and down to a long carbon chain which has 2 cis-configured double bonds and curves to the right. On the right, C3 bonds down and right to O, which bonds right to C, which double bonds up and right to O and down and right to a long carbon chain. The text at the bottom reads, "1-Stearoyl, 2-linoleoyl, 3-palmitoyl glycerol, a mixed triacylglycerol."

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing the structure of cholesterol. The strutcture of cholesterol has 3 parts: the polar head group, labeled left; the steroid nucleus, labeled middle; and the alkyl side chain, labeled right. Rings are labeled in pink A-D, beginning on the leftmost ring. The carbons are numbered beginning with the top carbon on the A ring. The A ring solid wedge bonds at carbon 3 on the lower right, to OH, which is shaded blue. This is the polar head group. The A ring bonds right to the B ring, which has a double bond between carbons 5 and 6. Between the tops of the two rings is a solid wedge bond that makes C19. At C9, there is a dashed wedge bond down to H, so that it reaches down into the B ring. The bond between C8 and C9 bonds up and right to the C ring. The C ring has a solid wedge bonded H on C8, the bottom point of the ring. Bonds between C13 and C14, to the right, bond to ring D, which has 5 sides. Between the tops of ring C and D is an upward solid wedge bond that makes C18. This ring region is the steroid nucleus, labeled below. At the apex of ring D at C17, C17 dashed wedge bonds up and right to H, and up to C20. This begins the alkyl side chain, labeled right. C20 dashed wedge bonds up and left to C21, solid wedge bonds up to H, and bonds up and right to the side chain, which contains C23-C27.

p:cNvPr.descr: Structures of various isoprenoid compounds or derivatives. (d) Ubiquinone, a mitochondrial electron carrier (coenzyme Q) (n= 4 to 8) (labeled left). Its left ring has 2 vertical double bonds. The top and bottom C are double bonded up and down to O. From the top, C double bonds up to O and left to C, which bonds left to CHO3 and double bonds down to C, which bonds left to CHO3 and down and right to C, which double bonds down to O and up & right to C, which bonds right to CH2 and double bonds up to C, which bonds up & right to CH3 and up & left to C. A pink dashed line bisects the bond between the ring and CH2. CH2 bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to C, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH2. To the right of this CH2 there is a dashed pink line bisecting the bond. To the right of the pink line is a portion of the chain in parentheses: CH2 bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to C and up to CH3. C bonds right to CH2. To the right is the closing parenthese with n on the outside, representing 4 to 8. The rest of the chain, to the right, consists of CH2 bonding right to CH, which double bonds right to C, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH3. Below is (e) plastoquinone, a chloroplast electron carrier (n = 4 to 8) (labeled left). Its left ring has 2 vertical double bonds. The top and bottom C are double bonded up & down to O. From the top, C double bonds up to O and left to C, which bonds left to CH3 and double bonds down to C, which bonds left to CH3 and down and right to C, which double bonds down to O and up and right to C, which bonds right to CH2 and double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to CH3, and up and left to C. A pink dashed line bisects the bond between the ring and CH2. CH2 bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to C, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH2. To the right of this CH2, there is a dashed pink line bisecting the bond. To the right of the pink line is a portion of the chain in parentheses: CH2 bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to C and up to CH3. C bonds right to CH2. To the right is the closing parentheses with n on the outside, representing 4 to 8. The rest of the chain, to the right, consists of CH2 bonding right to CH, which double bonds right to C, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH3. Below is (f) dolichol, a sugar carrier (n = 9 to 22) (labeled left). It consists of an OH bonded right to CH2. There is a dashed pink line bisecting this bond. CH2 bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH. CH bonds up to CH3 and right to CH2. To the right, there is another dashed pink line. To the right of the line re parentheses containing CH2 bonded right to CH, which double bonds right to C. C bonds up to CH3 and right to CH2. Here there are parentheses with the letter n outside it, representing any number from 9 to 22. To the right of this is another dashed pink line. To the right of the line is CH2 bonded right to CH, which double bonds to C, which bonds up to CH3 and right to CH3.
